ModuleName: 8 - Numerical Methods with SciPy and Curve Fitting

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics
Artifacts.Description: Outlines the full sequence of topics covered in the module—including SciPy fundamentals, root finding, numerical integration, interpolation, and curve fitting—serving as a syllabus-style reference that helps learners and instructors navigate the module's content and progression.

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics (HTML)
Artifacts.Description: An overview page listing the topics covered in Module 8, including the SciPy library, its relationship to NumPy, and its application to numerical methods and curve fitting in engineering; learners use it as a navigation guide to understand what will be taught and in what order.

Artifacts.Name: Applying Numerical Methods to Engineering Datasets
Artifacts.Description: This reading walks learners through end-to-end engineering data workflows—cleaning raw sensor data, selecting and applying numerical methods, and interpreting results—serving as a contextual overview of how individual techniques combine into realistic engineering pipelines.

Artifacts.Name: Introduction to SciPy for Numerical Computing
Artifacts.Description: This reading introduces the SciPy library within the Python scientific computing ecosystem, covering its major submodules, their engineering applications (stress analysis, curve fitting, differential equations), and how learners should set up and navigate SciPy for numerical work.

Artifacts.Name: Root Finding with scipy.optimize
Artifacts.Description: This reading explains the concept of root finding and demonstrates how to use scipy.optimize tools (such as brentq and fsolve) to locate function zeros, covering method selection, bracketing, convergence, and practical engineering use cases where analytical solutions are unavailable.

Artifacts.Name: Numerical Integration with scipy.integrate
Artifacts.Description: This reading covers numerical integration theory and practice using scipy.integrate, addressing both formula-based integration (quad) and data-based integration (trapezoid, Simpson's rule), with guidance on when and how to apply each tool to real engineering problems.

Artifacts.Name: Linear Curve Fitting with numpy.polyfit
Artifacts.Description: This reading teaches polynomial and linear curve fitting using numpy.polyfit, explaining how to model noisy experimental data with best-fit lines or polynomials, interpret coefficients, assess fit quality with R², and apply the workflow to engineering datasets.

Artifacts.Name: Nonlinear Curve Fitting with scipy.optimize.curve fit
Artifacts.Description: This reading covers nonlinear curve fitting using scipy.optimize.curve_fit, explaining how to define custom model functions (e.g., exponential, power-law), estimate parameters, interpret uncertainty via covariance, and apply the technique to engineering relationships that linear methods cannot capture.

Artifacts.Name: Residuals Analysis
Artifacts.Description: This reading explains residuals analysis as a method for evaluating curve-fit quality, teaching learners how to compute, plot, and interpret residuals to detect model inadequacy, bias, or violations of assumptions after fitting linear, polynomial, or nonlinear models.

Artifacts.Name: Applying Numerical Methods to Engineering Datasets
Artifacts.Description: This reading walks learners through end-to-end engineering data workflows—cleaning raw sensor data, selecting and applying numerical methods, and interpreting results—serving as a contextual capstone showing how individual numerical techniques integrate into complete engineering analysis pipelines.

Artifacts.Name: Drag-and-Drop Match
Artifacts.Description: Learners drag SciPy and NumPy function names to their matching input/output descriptions to reinforce recognition of key numerical methods functions, serving as a self-check activity within the module on numerical methods and curve fitting.
